sources.entry: Questions to ask the company during your interview

summary.one_liner: A categorized checklist of questions job applicants can ask interviewers about the role, tech practices, team, company, business, remote work, and compensation.
summary.what_it_does: This is a list of questions for tech job applicants to ask during interviews, grouped into sections such as The Role, Tech, The Team, The Company, Conflict, The Business, Remote Work, Compensation, and Time Off. It mixes things the applicant may want to see (good practices like CI/CD, version-controlled infrastructure, blameless incident analysis) with red flags to avoid (such as unclear on-call pay, lack of PTO clarity, or unresolved conflict handling). The README says the points are unordered and many may not apply to a given position. It advises not to ask everything, and to look up answers that are already published before asking. The list is also available in multiple translations, and contributors are invited to send pull requests with new questions.
use_cases: Preparing questions to ask at the end of a job interview
Spotting red flags in a prospective employer's engineering practices
Comparing job offers on on-call, PTO, and remote work policies
Checking a team's release, testing, and incident-handling culture
Evaluating company stability through funding and runway questions
Planning a first-month or trial-period conversation with a manager
notable: Organized into role, tech, team, company, social, conflict, business, remote work, compensation, and time-off sections
Includes translations into more than 20 languages
Written as a personal list that grew over time, with both desired practices and red flags
Points to other question collections such as The Joel Test and Julia Evans' interview questions
Advises applicants to find published answers before asking the interviewer
caveats: The README says the questions are unordered and many may not apply to a given job or work type
Some content is US-centric, such as 401k and visa questions, and may not fit other countries
The author notes that practices and organizations change often, so answers may go out of date
